surah.personality_title: Ash-Sharh — The Relieved Chest & The Inseparability of Ease from Trial
surah.personality_summary: Expansive, weightless, uplifting, mobilizing. A direct companion to Ad-Duha, celebrating the expansion of the prophetic heart, the removal of the crushing burden, and the exaltation of his remembrance. Enunciates the cosmic spiritual law that hardship does not merely precede ease, but accompanies it, urging relentless devotion upon completion of tasks.
surah.opening_ending_dynamic: Connects opening theme to terminal resolution.
surah.overview: Surah Ash-Sharh (The Consolation) is the 94th surah in the canonical muṣḥaf sequence, comprising 8 ayat. Classified as Makki.

ayahs.arabic_simple: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
ayahs.arabic_clean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الم نشرح لك صدرك
ayahs.translation_saheeh: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast
ayahs.translation_abdelhaleem: Did We not relieve your heart for you [Prophet]

ayahs.translation_saheeh: And We removed from you your burden
Which had weighed upon your back
ayahs.translation_abdelhaleem: that weighed so heavily on your back

ayahs.translation_saheeh: And raised high for you your repute
For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease
ayahs.translation_abdelhaleem: So truly where there is hardship there is also ease
truly where there is hardship there is also ease

ayahs.translation_saheeh: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship]
ayahs.translation_abdelhaleem: The moment you are freed [of one task] work on

ayahs.translation_saheeh: And to your Lord direct [your] longing
ayahs.translation_abdelhaleem: and turn to your Lord for everything
